title: Make quality gating policy configurable per-route and account tier
author: Jordan Lee
release_notes: Gating enforcement can now vary by route and account tier (self-serve vs enterprise). New default policy introduced; existing routes are backfilled to preserve current behavior. Console/Optimize APIs expose the effective policy used for a recommendation/change.
description:
Title: Make quality gating policy configurable per-route and account tier

Context
Today, quality gates are effectively “one size fits all” once the feature flag is enabled. This creates friction for:
- Self-serve routes where we want a fast smoke gate by default (DX) and escalated full gates for higher-risk diffs.
- Enterprise / regulated routes where we want stricter defaults (full gates always, tighter override rules) and explicit auditability.

This PR introduces a first-class gating policy object that can be resolved by (route_id, account_tier, model_family) with sane defaults. Enforcement remains defense-in-depth (Optimize apply boundary + rollout promotion), but now reads a consistent policy source.

What’s in this PR
1) Policy model + resolution
- Adds GatePolicy and GatePolicyBinding data model.
- Resolution order:
  1. Route override (route_id)
  2. Tier default (account_tier)
  3. Global default
- Optional predicates for model_family and change_type (batching/cache/quant_profile).

2) Default policies (MVP)
- global_default: smoke gate required for apply; full gate required for canary promotion.
- tier:self_serve: smoke required; full required only for quant_profile changes.
- tier:enterprise: full required for all in-scope change types.

3) Enforcement wiring
- Optimize ApplyConfig endpoint now loads effective policy and enforces required gate tier(s).
- Rollout controller promotion check reads the same effective policy for the route/tier.
- Override flow unchanged but now validates against policy (e.g., enterprise requires explicit approver role).

4) Console/Optimize API surface
- Gate run summary endpoints now include "effective_policy" metadata (id + human-readable summary + resolved_from).
- Allows UI to explain “why you’re blocked” and what gate tier is required.

5) Migration/backfill
- Introduces a migration to create global_default and tier defaults.
- Backfills existing gating-enabled routes to a route binding matching the prior behavior to avoid surprise changes.

Out of scope
- Private/on-prem automation policy distribution (this will be design-only for now).
- Per-account custom policies beyond tier (we can add account_id bindings later if needed).

Testing
- Unit tests for policy resolution ordering and fallbacks.
- Integration tests for apply boundary enforcement by tier.
- Added a small e2e fixture to ensure rollout promotion is blocked when policy requires full gates.

Example (sanitized)
- Policy summary string shown in API responses:
  "tier=enterprise -> require_full_gate_for=[batching,cache,quant_profile], require_smoke_gate_for=[batching,cache,quant_profile], overrides=admin_or_enterprise_approver"

Rollout plan
- Ship policy plumbing + defaults behind existing gating feature flag.
- For limited production rollout, only apply tier defaults for newly created routes; existing routes remain pinned via backfill bindings.

Follow-ups
- Add account_id bindings once we have a stable enterprise exceptions workflow (see PM-482).
- Add policy observability counters (policy_resolution_source, required_tier) once ENG-3926 lands.

Refs
- Related PRs: pr-19531 (block apply when gate fails), pr-19544 (rollout controller respects gate), pr-19537 (override flow)
- Linear: ENG-3921, ENG-3928; PM: PM-481
commits: policy: add GatePolicy + GatePolicyBinding models and DAO
policy: implement resolver (route -> tier -> global) with model/change_type matching
optimize: enforce required gate tier(s) on apply boundary using resolved policy
rollouts: enforce promotion requirements using resolved policy
api: include effective policy summary + resolved_from in gate run responses
migrations: seed defaults + backfill existing routes to preserve prior behavior
tests: policy resolution unit tests + apply/rollout integration tests
conversation:
Aditya Rao (Product) — 2026-02-10
Can we make sure existing customers don’t see behavior changes on rollout? I’m worried enterprise routes might suddenly require full gates and block planned changes.

Jordan Lee (Author) — 2026-02-10
Yep. The backfill migration creates route-level bindings for any route that previously had gating enabled, mapping to the old behavior. Tier defaults will only apply to new routes unless we explicitly migrate them.

Paula Mendes — 2026-02-10
For rollout coupling: does the rollout controller use the same resolver or are we duplicating logic?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-10
Same resolver logic, shared contract via a lightweight policy summary record fetched from Optimize. For now rollout controller calls Optimize’s policy endpoint (with caching) to avoid drift.

Noah Patel — 2026-02-11
Request: add static validation so a policy can’t require “full” without “smoke” (or define what that means). Also ensure quant_profile always forces at least smoke even on global default.

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-11
Added validation: required_full implies required_smoke for the same change types (enforced at write + migration seed). Also added a guardrail: quant_profile change types always require >= smoke even if misconfigured.

Benji Okafor — 2026-02-11
DB review: do we need an index on (route_id, account_tier, model_family)? Resolver will run per apply.

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-11
Added composite indexes on bindings: (route_id, precedence), (account_tier, precedence) and (model_family, change_type). Also caching in Optimize for 30s with invalidation on policy write.

Dylan Brooks — 2026-02-12
Console needs to show a clear human-readable explanation. Can you include “resolved_from” so UI can say “Route override” vs “Enterprise default”?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-12
Done. Response now includes resolved_from in {route_override|tier_default|global_default} and a summary string (kept stable for UI copy).

Sean Gallagher — 2026-02-12
SRE ask: please emit a counter for policy resolution failures / fallbacks. If Optimize can’t resolve, we should fail closed for enterprise, but not for self-serve?

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-12
Implemented fail-closed across all tiers when gating is enabled (consistent with guardrails goal). Added structured logs for resolution failures and a metric stub behind the existing gating metrics feature flag (full dashboards in ENG-3926).

Paula Mendes — 2026-02-13
Looks good. One more: rollout controller should treat “policy endpoint unavailable” as promotion blocked (not allowed).

Jordan Lee — 2026-02-13
Confirmed: promotion check returns BLOCKED with reason QUALITY_GATE_POLICY_UNAVAILABLE and surfaces it in the rollout event.
